BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r9.claim: The claim that Paradise alone is the person’s abode seems too exclusive if a sinful believer first enters Hell; Bursevi resolves this by taking the exclusivity to mean that whoever enters Paradise never leaves it.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r9.anchor: قد يدخل النار أو لا ثم يدخل الجنة فلا يصح في حقه الحصر

QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.claim: The one fearing the Lord’s station ascends to heart and witnesses divine governance, restrains the self from desire through fear or awe, and reaches paradise according to rank.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.anchor: بالترقي إلى مقام القلب ومشاهدة قيوميته تعالى على نفسه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.claim: The passage contrasts the rebellious and disobedient people’s fate with glad tidings for those who feared God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.anchor: A mention of the fate of the rebellious and the disobedient on the Day of Judgement.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r1.claim: For the person who restrains desire, Paradise alone is the final abode; the contrast apparently applies to all people of the Fire and of Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r1.anchor: له لا غيرها والظاهر أن هذا التفصيل عام في أهل النار وأهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two verses concern the brothers Abu ʿAziz and Musʿab: one was tyrannical and worldly, while Musʿab feared God and restrained desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.anchor: أن الآيتين نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير وأخيه مصعب بن عمير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.claim: Musʿab protected the Prophet at Uhud and died pierced by arrows; the Prophet said he entrusted him to God and recalled his two cloaks and golden sandal strap.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.anchor: وقد وقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنفسه يوم أحد حين تفرق الناس عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf says Musʿab killed his captured brother Abu ʿAziz at Uhud; the account says their mother was exceptionally wealthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.anchor: وفي الكشاف أنه قتل أخاه أبا عزيز يوم أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas connects the two verses to Abu Jahl and Musʿab; another says the first verse concerned al-Nadr and his son al-Harith.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنهما نزلتا في أبي جهل وفي مصعب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r6.claim: For that person, Paradise is the final shelter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r6.anchor: فإن الجنة هي المأوى يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r1.claim: Paradise is the only abode for the person who restrains desire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r1.anchor: { فإن الجنة هى المأوى } ليس له سواها مأوى

NAHHAS:v5p146/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r10.claim: The parsing is like the one just given.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r9.claim: Paradise alone is the watchful believer’s final home and reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r9.anchor: أي البستان الجامع لكل ما يشتهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.claim: The warning and glad tidings follow the proof of resurrection because judgment follows resurrection; the wise prepare for lasting reward rather than transient pleasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.anchor: فإن إثبات البعث يقتضي الجزاء إذ هو حكمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r8.claim: The definite articles in the two ‘abode’ phrases refer back to the abode of each group; Basran and Kufan grammarians differ over whether the article replaces an omitted possessive or modifies an implied possessive construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r8.anchor: والتعريف في { المأوى } الأول والثاني تعريف العهد ، أي مأوى من طغى ، ومأوى من خاف مقام ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r1.claim: Ma'wa is a place noun from ‘return’; it means a person's settled dwelling, where one returns after attending to other affairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r1.anchor: والمأوى : اسم مكان من أوى ، إذا رجع ، فالمراد به : المقر والمسكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.claim: The paired descriptions of remembering and the Garden use a collect-then-divide rhetorical structure; ‘the self’ has the same generic definite sense as ‘the abode.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.anchor: وفي قوله : { يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى } إلى قوله : { فإن الجنة هي المأوى } محسن الجمع مع التقسيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r4.claim: Describing the people of Fire and Garden with relative clauses hints that each clause is the cause of its group deserving that abode.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r4.anchor: وفي تعريف ( أصحاب الجحيم ) و ( أصحاب الجنة ) بطريق الموصول إيماء إلى أن الصلتين علتان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.claim: المأوى is the dwelling where someone settles and remains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.anchor: والمأوى والمسكن حيث يأوي المرء ويلازم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r6.claim: The person who restrains desire will return to Paradise as his final abode.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r6.anchor: أي: منقلبه ومصيره ومرجعه إلى الجنة الفيحاء.

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.claim: The verses distinguish obedience from rebellion: Paradise is attained through obedience and Hell deserved for sins, against the determinists' claim.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.anchor: تبيين حال المطيع من حال العاصي، وأن الجنة تنال بالطاعة، والنار تستحق بالمعاصي

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.claim: The Garden is earned by preferring obedience and avoiding sins; the command to restrain the self from desire includes both.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.anchor: أن الجنة تنال بإيثار الطاعة، والاجتناب عن المعاصي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.claim: One report says these verses were revealed about Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Mus'ab ibn Umayr: Mus'ab killed his brother at Uhud and defended the Messenger until struck by arrows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير ، وقد قتل مصعب أخاه أبا عزير يوم أحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.claim: The refuge is the Garden, meaning one's dwelling; the verse is said to have been revealed about Musab ibn Umayr.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.anchor: { فإن الجنة هي المأوى } أي المنزل , وذكر أنها نزلت في مصعب بن عمير .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#2/r1.claim: Paradise is the destination and place of return.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r14.anchor: أي المنزل. والآيتان نزلتا في مصعب بن عمير وأخيه عامر بن عمير

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.claim: The two verses concern Mus'ab ibn Umayr and his brother Amir: Amir was captured at Badr, identified himself as Mus'ab's brother, and was initially treated kindly until Mus'ab ordered the captors to bind him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.anchor: أما من طغى فهو أخ لمصعب بن عمير أسر يوم بدر، فأخذته الأنصار

ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.claim: The poet’s “lower the gaze” addresses a man whose gaze is meant; this supports reading al-maʾwā as “his refuge” for both Hell and Paradise.
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: فغض الطرف إنك من نمير. . . فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.claim: Fear of one's Lord counters transgression, while restraining desire counters preferring worldly life; fear depends on knowledge (35:28) and causes restraint, so cause precedes effect.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.anchor: ولما كان الخوف من الله هو السبب المعين لدفع الهوى

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.claim: The two descriptions encompass all virtues, just as the paired descriptions of Hell's people encompass all vices.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.anchor: وكما دخل في ذينك الصفتين جميع القبائح

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.claim: A reported occasion links the verses to Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Musab ibn Umayr: Musab killed his brother at Uhud and shielded the Prophet until pierced by spears.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.claim: Verses 34–41 contrast believers' and disbelievers' outcomes on Resurrection Day.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.anchor: returns to a description of the Day of Resurrection, contrasting the fate of the believers with that of the disbelievers

TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r2.claim: For such a person, Paradise is the abode and residence on Resurrection Day; al-Ṭabarī refers to his earlier discussion of the same phrase in 55:46.
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r2.anchor: فإن الجنة هي مأواه ومنزله يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.claim: The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.anchor: وهناك غير الطائفتين طوائف أخر من المستضعفين والذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.claim: In “the refuge,” the definite article can replace a possessive pronoun, or an omitted pronoun can be supplied: it means the refuge for him.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.anchor: على أن تكون اللام عوضا عن الضمير أو الضمير محذوف والتقدير هي المأوى له

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.speaker: محمد الباقر
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.claim: Qummi reports al-Baqir saying that a servant who can commit a sin but leaves it from fear of God and His prohibition is rewarded with Paradise.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.anchor: قال هو العبد إذ وقف على معصية الله وقدر عليها ثم تركها مخافة الله ونهي الله

TABRISI:79:27-46/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:79:27-46/r6.claim: The abode phrase has an understood “for him”; another grammarian says the definite article substitutes for the returning pronoun, meaning his abode.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: وقال قوم الألف واللام بدل من الضمير العائد

TABRISI:79:45-46/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r8.claim: For the person who fears God and restrains desire, Paradise is the final home and refuge.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r8.anchor: { فإن الجنة هي المأوى } له أي هي مقره ومأواه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.claim: These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.anchor: Bu birkaç kısa âyette âhiretteki büyük kaybı veya büyük kurtuluşu hazırlayan olumsuz ve olumlu tutumların çok veciz bir özeti yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.claim: Those who expect to answer to God set aside passing desires and live responsibly; they are promised great reward and salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.anchor: Allah’ın huzurunda dünyada yaşadığı hayatın hesabını vereceğini düşünerek geçici heveslerini bir yana bırakıp sorumlu bir hayat geçirenlerin büyük ödüle ve kurtuluşa kavuşacakları müjdelenmektedir

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads “seven letters” as seven Arabic tongues; the seven gates of Paradise stand for Quranic content—commands, prohibitions, exhortation, warning, stories, and parables—whose observance merits Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: والسبعة الأحرف، هو ما قلنا من أنه الألسن السبعة، والأبواب السبعة من الجنة، هي المعاني التي فيها من الأمر، والنهي، والترغيب، والترهيب، والقصص، والمثل

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites reports he calls established through ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy and others: they disputed recitation, and the Prophet approved each reading and said God commanded seven letters.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، وعبد الله بن مسعود، وأبي بن كعب، وسائر من قد قدمنا الرواية عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: He argues that approving variants with different legal or doctrinal meanings would force God to command, forbid, and permit the same act, so the recitations cannot conflict in meaning.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: لو كان تماريا واختلافا فيما دلت عليه تلاواتهم من التحليل، والتحريم، والوعد، والوعيد، وما أشبه ذلك، لكان مستحيلا أن يصوب جميعهم صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī invokes Q 4:82: because the Quran denies extensive contradiction in itself, it cannot prescribe divergent rulings through variant readings.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r4.anchor: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r5.claim: He adds that the Prophet never ruled one matter at one time by two opposing judgments or authorized this for his community, which also excludes semantic disagreement among readings.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r5.anchor: مع أن في قيام الحجة بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لم يقض في شيء واحد، في وقت واحد بحكمين مختلفين، ولا أذن بذلك لأمته

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r6.claim: Since the disputants already accepted God's commands, prohibitions, promises, warnings, prophetic arguments, admonition, and parables, their objection must have concerned wording and language.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r6.anchor: فما الوجه الذي أوجب له إنكاره ما أنكر إن لم يكن كان ذلك اختلافا منهم في الألفاظ واللغات؟

TAB-FULL:v1p43/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r7.speaker: من خالف قولنا في ذلك
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the opposing interpretation that the seven letters signified seven divergent meanings, since that would affirm contradiction in the Quran and deny its coherence.
TAB-FULL:v1p43/r7.anchor: فساد تأويل قول من خالف قولنا في ذلك

BURHAN:v1p63/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.claim: The author suggests the singular “Paradise” in 79:41 may have driven al-Farrāʾ’s rhyme explanation, but the dual “both with branches” remains an objection to it.
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.anchor: قلت وكأن الملجىء للفراء إلى ذلك قوله تعالى ﴿ وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى ﴾

BURHAN:v4p37/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.claim: The definite article can stand in for a pronoun: Hell is its refuge for the one who preferred worldly life, while Paradise is the refuge for the one who feared God.
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.anchor: فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى

BURHAN:v4p37/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.claim: The Kufans explain the definite article in these refuge phrases as a substitute for the omitted pronoun.
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.anchor: وقول الكوفيين الألف واللام عوض من الضمير

ITQAN:v2p441/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p441/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
ITQAN:v2p441/r1.claim: Kufans, some Basrans, and many later grammarians let the definite article stand for a possessive pronoun in ‘the Garden is the refuge’; opponents supply the pronoun in their parsing.
ITQAN:v2p441/r1.anchor: أجاز الكوفيون وبعض البصريين وكثير من المتأخرين نيابة أل عن الضمير المضاف إليه

ITQAN:v3p268/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r5.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v3p268/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the dual jannatān here means one garden, as in al-janna hiya al-maʾwā, and that two men are called ashqāhā in the other example; he attributes the forms to rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p268/r5.anchor: قال الفراء أراد ( جنة ) كقوله ﴿ فإن الجنة هي المأوى ﴾ فثنى لأجل الفاصلة قال والقوافي تحتمل من الزيادة والنقصان ما لا يحتمله سائر الكلام

FARRA:v3p232/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r11.claim: Paradise is the abode of those who feared their Lord and restrained themselves from desire.
FARRA:v3p232/r11.anchor: من وصفناه بما وصفناه به من خوف ربه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن جرير الطبري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari argues that the Qur’an descended in some Arab tongues, not all, since Arab tongues and dialects number more than seven and cannot be counted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r2.anchor: قال الإمام أبو جعفر بن جرير الطبري، رحمه الله، بعد ما أورد طرفا مما تقدم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r3.claim: The discussion asks what evidence supports the dialect account of the seven letters over the alternate view that they mean commands, prohibitions, exhortation, warnings, stories, and parables.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r3.anchor: وما برهانك على ما قلته دون أن يكون معناه ما قاله مخالفوك، من أنه نزل بأمر وزجر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says advocates of the thematic explanation do not claim that it is the meaning of the earlier reports about seven letters; they mean the Qur’an came in seven aspects, as transmitted from the Prophet and Companions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r4.anchor: إن الذين قالوا ذلك لم يدعوا أن تأويل الأخبار التي تقدم ذكرها، هو ما زعمت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r5.claim: Reports from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿud say the Qur’an descended from seven gates of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r5.anchor: في رواية عن أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود: أن القرآن نزل من سبعة أبواب الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن جرير الطبري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari explains the seven gates as the Qur’an’s meanings—commands, prohibitions, encouragement, warning, stories, and parables—which lead those who practice them to Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p42#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن جرير: والأبواب السبعة من الجنة هي المعاني التي فيها من الأمر والنهي
